messages.author: 484c91357ac83f6b
messages.subject: D_GLIBCXX_DEBUG
parts:
While I was checking the branch feature/fix-issue-575-to-matrix for
problems yesterday, I realized that a test that passed a while ago
didn't pass this time:

make test/unit/math/matrix/containers_conversion

The reason was that I have started including the flag -D_GLIBCXX_DEBUG:

make test/unit/math/matrix/containers_conversion CC="g++ -D_GLIBCXX_DEBUG"

Which makes the operator vec[n] of std::vector check if n is in the
bounds of vec just like vec.at(n) does

It turns out that this flag helped me catch this error:
to_matrix(const vector< vector<T> > & vec) {
vector<int> RC = dims(vec);
int R = RC[0];
int C = RC[1];
...
}
to_matrix(some_empty_vector_of_vectors);


It seems that whenever vec is an empty vector, dims(vec)[1] doesn't
exists, but this doesn't cause segmentation fault and the behavior of
the function will be unexpected.

So, I wonder, would this flag be useful for testing with Jenkins?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] D_GLIBCXX_DEBUG [helpful for Jenkins testing?]
parts:
On May 17, 2014, at 7:21 PM, Marco Inacio <marcoig...@gmail.com> wrote:

> While I was checking the branch feature/fix-issue-575-to-matrix for problems yesterday, I realized that a test that passed a while ago didn't pass this time:
>
> make test/unit/math/matrix/containers_conversion
>
> The reason was that I have started including the flag -D_GLIBCXX_DEBUG:
>
> make test/unit/math/matrix/containers_conversion CC="g++ -D_GLIBCXX_DEBUG"
> So, I wonder, would this flag be useful for testing with Jenkins?

> Which makes the operator vec[n] of std::vector check if n is in the bounds of vec just like vec.at(n) does
>
> It turns out that this flag helped me catch this error:
> to_matrix(const vector< vector<T> > & vec) {
> vector<int> RC = dims(vec);
> int R = RC[0];
> int C = RC[1];
> ...
> }
> to_matrix(some_empty_vector_of_vectors);
> It seems that whenever vec is an empty vector, dims(vec)[1] doesn't exists, but this doesn't cause segmentation fault and the behavior of the function will be unexpected.

Right --- there aren't any further dims here. We could probably
finesse dims() to fill out zeroes.

Nevertheless, this is not a good way to implement to_matrix because
of the unnecessary creation of RC. Vectors aren't cheap to create,
destroy, or assign (at least prior to C++11), because they have mallocs
under the hood.

Why not just use this:

for (size_t i = 0; i < vec.size(); ++i)
for (size_t j = 0; j < vec[i].size(); ++j)
mat(i,j) = vec[i][j];

There's no way to get better memory locality because
mat will be organized column-maor and the vec of vecs
row major.

- Bob
